observations.behavior: Adds documentation and metadata for three new MCP tools: archive, disable, enable, unarchive, and updates the description of update-feature-flag.
observations.code_quote:
"description": "Archive a feature flag, hiding it from the default flag list. Requires the flag's numeric ID; use `feature-flag-get-definition-by-key` to get it from a key, or `feature-flag-get-all` to search by key or name.

Sets `archived` to true. An archived flag must be disabled, so an enabled flag is turned off in the same call. Nothing else changes: this tool never accepts or replaces the `filters` object, and linked experiment and survey history is preserved. There is no request body.

When the flag is enabled, archiving stops it evaluating everywhere. Tell the user what else this affects: linked experiments, surveys, early access features and session replay settings all appear in the flag's full definition.

Returns 400 when the flag is enabled and other active flags depend on it. Returns 409 when an approval policy gates disabling. Archiving an already-archived flag succeeds and changes nothing, so retrying is safe.

A key lookup that finds nothing does not mean the flag is absent. Archived flags are hidden from `feature-flag-get-definition-by-key` and from `feature-flag-get-all`, so a flag that is already archived looks missing on a retry. Pass `{"archived":"true"}` to `feature-flag-get-all` before you report the flag as missing.

Use `feature-flag-unarchive` to put the flag back in the list, or `delete-feature-flag` when the user wants it gone rather than tidied away.",

observations.behavior: Adds four new MCP tool handlers and their Zod schemas for archive, disable, enable, unarchive, and updates the tool registry and documentation.
observations.code_quote:
"description": "Update a feature flag by numeric ID (partial update: only the fields you include are changed). Use this for edits that have no dedicated tool, such as release conditions, rollout percentages, variants, payloads, tags and the description.

Prefer a dedicated tool whenever the request matches one. `feature-flag-enable`, `feature-flag-disable`, `feature-flag-archive` and `feature-flag-unarchive` each change one state field and send no `filters`. A targeting change someone else made between your read and your write is therefore not overwritten. Send `active` or `archived` here only when the same request also changes targeting or another field, so the whole edit lands in one write.

Rollout conditions, variants, and payloads live in the structured `filters` param, and sending `filters` replaces the whole object, so read the flag first and merge your change. Use `feature-flag-get-definition-by-key` when you have the string key: it returns the numeric ID and the full definition in one call. Use `feature-flag-get-definition` when you already have the ID. To apply a change at a future time instead, use `scheduled-changes-create`.",
